# Press freedom group calls for ICE to release Afghan journalist from California detention
An international press freedom group has called on U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to release and grant asylum to an Afghan journalist who is being held in a California detention facility.
Shaban Ali Rafat has been held in ICE detention since he entered the U.S. in January 2025 and authorities have sought to deport him back to Afghanistan, where he faces the risk of being tortured, according to his attorney.
The Committee to Protect Journalists this month [urged authorities](https://cpj.org/2026/11/cpj-calls-on-us-immigration-authorities-to-release-afghan-journalist-grant-full-access-to-asylum/) to “immediately and unconditionally release” Rafat and grant him asylum. The organization warned that deporting Rafat to Afghanistan would expose him to “significant risks of persecution and retaliation” by the Taliban, both because of his work as a journalist and because he is a member of Afghanistan’s Hazara ethnic minority group.

“Rafat fled Afghanistan because the Taliban made it impossible for him to work as a journalist without risking his life. Deporting him now would deliver him directly into the hands of the very persecutors he escaped,” Jose Zamora, the Committee to Protect Journalists Americas regional program director, said in a statement.

On Nov. 6, a magistrate for the United States District Court for the Eastern District of California [recommended his release.](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.caed.496939/gov.uscourts.caed.496939.10.0.pdf) Still, Rafat remains in detention and is scheduled for a court hearing in his immigration case Dec. 8.

# CPJ Urges Release of Afghan Journalist as US Court Reviews Prolonged Detention
![CPJ Urges Release of Afghan Journalist as US Court Reviews Prolonged Detention](https://asiadaily.org/media/uploads/2026/11/18773-1858389471.webp)
## Nearly 22 months in custody, with a warning against return
Afghan journalist Shaban Ali Rafat remained in US immigration custody nearly 22 months after seeking asylum, even as a federal magistrate judge recommended his release and a protection assessment found he would more likely than not face torture if returned to Afghanistan.

The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) called on November 13, 2026, for his immediate and unconditional release and a full hearing on his asylum claim. His attorney, David Tarr, said Rafat faces deportation to Afghanistan, where his journalism and membership of the Hazara minority place him at risk.
Rafat has been held by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in California since January 21, 2025, when he attempted to enter the United States to seek asylum. On November 6, a magistrate judge recommended granting his challenge to continued detention and releasing him under supervision, finding that his detention had become unreasonable.

CPJ's [November 13 statement](https://cpj.org/2026/11/cpj-calls-on-us-immigration-authorities-to-release-afghan-journalist-grant-full-access-to-asylum/) asks ICE to release Rafat and give him full access to a hearing on the merits of his asylum claim. Such a hearing would examine the substance of his case, including the persecution he fears and the evidence supporting his request for protection.

# Press freedom group calls for ICE to release Afghan journalist from California detention
An international press freedom group has called on U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to release and grant asylum to an Afghan journalist who is being held in a California detention facility.
Shaban Ali Rafat has been held in ICE detention since he entered the U.S. in January 2025 and authorities have sought to deport him back to Afghanistan, where he faces the risk of being tortured, according to his attorney.
The Committee to Protect Journalists this month [urged authorities](https://cpj.org/2026/11/cpj-calls-on-us-immigration-authorities-to-release-afghan-journalist-grant-full-access-to-asylum/) to “immediately and unconditionally release” Rafat and grant him asylum. The organization warned that deporting Rafat to Afghanistan would expose him to “significant risks of persecution and retaliation” by the Taliban, both because of his work as a journalist and because he is a member of Afghanistan’s Hazara ethnic minority group.

“Rafat fled Afghanistan because the Taliban made it impossible for him to work as a journalist without risking his life. Deporting him now would deliver him directly into the hands of the very persecutors he escaped,” Jose Zamora, the Committee to Protect Journalists Americas regional program director, said in a statement.

On Nov. 6, a magistrate for the United States District Court for the Eastern District of California [recommended his release.](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.caed.496939/gov.uscourts.caed.496939.10.0.pdf) Still, Rafat remains in detention and is scheduled for a court hearing in his immigration case Dec. 8.

# CPJ calls on US immigration authorities to release Afghan journalist, grant full access to asylum

November 13, 2026 5:45 PM EST

New York, November 13, 2026—The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement authorities to immediately and unconditionally release Afghan journalist Shaban Ali Rafat and grant him full access to a hearing on the merits of his asylum claim. CPJ warns that deporting Rafat to Afghanistan would expose him to significant risks of persecution and retaliation by the Taliban. 

Rafat has been in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody in California since January 21, 2025, when he attempted to enter the United States to seek asylum, and now faces deportation to Afghanistan, according to his attorney David Tarr. 

“Rafat fled Afghanistan because the Taliban made it impossible for him to work as a journalist without risking his life. Deporting him now would deliver him directly into the hands of the very persecutors he escaped,” said CPJ Americas regional program director Jose Zamora. “His prolonged detention is a betrayal of the United States’ commitments to press freedom and human rights. U.S. authorities must release Rafat and provide him with asylum.” 

Before the Taliban takeover of Afghanistan in August 2021, Rafat worked as a producer and reporter for state-owned Maaref TV and served as a senior media officer at Kabul University, where he extensively covered the 2020 terrorist attack on the university and the plight of the Hazara community — a persecuted ethnic and religious minority of which he is a member.

Afghanistan’s Hazara community has faced escalating persecution and violence since the Taliban’s return to power in August 2021. In 2026 alone, the Taliban shut down three Hazara media outlets, and detained their senior managers in an effort to suppress the community’s media outlets and journalists in Afghanistan.
